resources.string: A screen-time self-control test. It checks only the name of the current app and shows a blocking screen for the selected app. It does not read screen text, messages, or page content. It is not an accessibility aid. You can revoke access at any time.
This separate test blocks one non-system app after 30 seconds of use. App usage access and the Accessibility service are required. Exercise counting and daily budgets are not active yet.
App usage access is unavailable; limits are not enforced.
Service access is unavailable; limits are not enforced.
Service is not connected; limits are not enforced. Check Accessibility settings.
Test is active; waiting for the selected app to be used
If Android has restricted access, check “Allow restricted settings” in the app info screen or its menu. The option’s name and location may vary by phone.
No selectable non-system apps were found. This test currently skips system and preinstalled apps.
Starting a new test resets the trial timer. This is for testing only and will not be used in the app’s real budget.
The 30 seconds of use have elapsed. Go home and open another app; returning to this app should block it again. Exercise and rewards are not active yet.
Go to the phone’s home screen
Could not show the blocking screen; limits are not enforced. Stop the test and check service access.
Could not save the time, so the test stopped. Limits may not be reliable.
The selected app can no longer be tested. Stop the test and choose another app.
The service was interrupted. Stop the test and check the connection.
Could not navigate. Use the phone’s Home button or gesture, or stop the test.
Could not complete this action. Check phone settings, permissions, and the service connection.
